chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Abu Saeed al-Mukari, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

I was at the fountain of Zamzam, and a man came to me and said to me, 'Do not drink from this water, O Abu Hamza, for in this the Jinn and humans share, and in this only humans share.' I was surprised by his statement and said, 'From where does he know this?' Then I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) what the man had said to me, so he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'That man is from the Jinn, intending to guide you.'

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ): Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about the man who advised Abu Hamza at Zamzam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the subtle interplay between the unseen world and human ritual practices, specifically regarding the sanctity and accessibility of Zamzam water. Imam al-Sadiq’s confirmation that the advisor was a Jinn underscores the Shia belief in the active, albeit often hidden, presence of Jinn in daily life and their capacity to offer guidance or mislead humans, reinforcing the need for spiritual discernment.
